ActivityConfig.description:
``[activity]`` — the durable audit/activity store (see hal0.activity).

Records every config-mutating action and system state change to a SQLite
table that survives restarts. ``retention_days`` and ``max_rows`` keep the
DB bounded without losing recent history. ``HAL0_ACTIVITY_RETENTION_DAYS``
overrides retention at the env layer.

``extra="forbid"`` (P3-schema Part C): a leaf tunable table. Previously
had no explicit ``model_config`` (pydantic's default is ``"ignore"``, not
``"allow"``) -- made explicit here rather than left implicit.

enabled.description: Whether config-mutating actions and system state changes are recorded to the durable activity store. Consumed once at create_app(), so a change needs a hal0-api restart.
enabled.title: Enabled

max_rows.description: Row cap for the activity table; oldest rows are pruned past this count regardless of retention_days. Set to 0 to disable the cap (retention_days still applies).
max_rows.title: Max Rows

retention_days.description: How long an activity row survives before pruning. Overridden at the env layer by HAL0_ACTIVITY_RETENTION_DAYS.
retention_days.title: Retention Days

ActivityConfig.title: ActivityConfig

BrainChatConfig.description:
``[brain_chat]`` — the dashboard's agent-chat steward (hal0-brain).

Guardrails and loop tuning for the slide-out chat that administers the
instance through tools (slots, models, benchmarks, the Operator Board).

``enabled`` is a hard kill switch: when false the endpoint refuses every
turn, so the steward chat is off. ``read_only`` keeps the chat answering
and reading state but refuses every mutating or admin-write tool
server-side — a guardrail that holds INDEPENDENTLY of the ``hal0-brain``
persona's ``tools_allowed`` / approval policy (a persona edit can loosen
the persona, never this). ``model`` overrides which model/slot the chat
drives (e.g. ``hal0/npu`` to run the steward on the NPU chat slot); empty
keeps the persona's ``preferred_model`` (``hal0/brain``, which itself
falls back to the ``agent`` slot). ``max_rounds`` bounds the per-turn tool
loop (runaway backstop); ``completion_timeout_s`` is the transport timeout
for each LLM round against the target slot.

Context floor (fresh-box finding, docs/rework/r4-stage-validation.md
"steward config note"): whichever slot ends up serving the chat --
``model`` here, the persona's ``preferred_model``, or the ``hal0/brain``
-> ``agent`` resolver fallback -- MUST be loaded with at least 8k tokens
of context. The built-in hal0-brain system prompt alone is ~7.3k tokens
before any conversation history or tool schemas are added; a smaller
context window truncates the prompt and the steward degrades silently
(malformed tool calls, prompt-following failures) rather than failing
loudly. Separately, a ``model`` (or resolver fallback) that resolves to
NO loaded slot at all 404s the self ``/v1/chat/completions`` call
outright -- surfaced by :mod:`hal0.brain.chat` as an actionable SSE
``error`` frame (naming the model tried and how to fix it) rather than
the raw transport failure.

``extra="forbid"`` (P3-schema Part C): a leaf tunable table. Previously
had no explicit ``model_config`` (pydantic's default is ``"ignore"``, not
``"allow"``) -- made explicit here rather than left implicit.

completion_timeout_s.description: Transport timeout (seconds) for each LLM round against the target slot. A round that exceeds this fails the turn with a timeout error instead of hanging indefinitely.
completion_timeout_s.title: Completion Timeout S

enabled.description: Hard kill switch for the dashboard's agent-chat steward. When false, every chat turn is refused and the slide-out chat is off.
enabled.title: Enabled

max_rounds.description: Runaway backstop: max tool-calling rounds in one chat turn before the steward stops and returns whatever it has.
max_rounds.title: Max Rounds

model.description: Which model/slot drives the steward chat. Empty keeps the persona's preferred_model (hal0/brain, itself falling back to the agent slot); set to a virtual slot like 'hal0/npu' to pin the steward there. Whatever this resolves to must be loaded with >= 8k context, or the chat fails outright.
model.title: Model

read_only.description: When true (the shipped default), the steward answers and reads state but every mutating or admin-write tool is refused server-side — independently of the persona's own tool policy. The steward's own memory_add into its private namespace is the one exception (#2658). Set false to let the steward act on the instance through tools.
read_only.title: Read Only

tool_model.description: Where a tool-calling ROUND reroutes when the chat model can't emit tool calls this runtime parses. Default 'hal0/agent' — the always-on fallback anchor — but that slot ships unbound on a fresh install, so the first tool turn has nowhere to go until an operator pulls a model into it. Per-round, not per-conversation: plain chat stays on 'model'. An empty string is coerced back to the default with a warning — to genuinely disable tool routing, set 'off', 'none', or 'disabled'.
tool_model.title: Tool Model

BrainChatConfig.title: BrainChatConfig

BridgeConfig.description:
``[bridge]`` — the agent bridge for remote coding agents (ADR-0043).

The bridge lets a remote coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, a CI job)
reach hal0's MCP servers and delegate to Hermes with its own revocable
``hal0bk_`` key. ``enabled`` defaults on because the surface is inert
until an operator adds a client (ADR-0043): the mount and ``/api/bridge/*``
exist on every box, but with no client rows nothing except the admin key
can authenticate, so onboarding stays one command with no restart.

``extra="forbid"`` (P3-schema Part C leaf-table policy, same as
``[network]``): a typo'd key must fail loudly instead of silently leaving
a limit at its default.

clarify_timeout_s.description: How long, in seconds, a run waits for the calling agent to answer a clarifying question from Hermes before the run is stopped with 'clarification unanswered' (60 to 3600). Applies to the next question, no restart.
clarify_timeout_s.title: Clarify Timeout S

enabled.description: Master switch for the agent bridge. Off = no bridge key authenticates, the bridge MCP server is not mounted, and adding, rotating or re-scoping a client and GET /api/bridge/me answer 404 bridge.disabled; listing and revoking clients keep working. On is harmless until you add a client: with no clients, nothing but the admin key can authenticate. Applies at the next hal0-api restart.
enabled.title: Enabled

max_concurrent_runs_per_client.description: How many Hermes runs one bridge client may have in flight at once (1 to 16). A start request past the limit is refused until one of its runs finishes. Applies on the next start request, no restart.
max_concurrent_runs_per_client.title: Max Concurrent Runs Per Client

run_retention_days.description: How many days bridge runs and their recorded events are kept before the maintenance pass deletes them (1 to 365). Applies on the next pass, no restart.
run_retention_days.title: Run Retention Days

BridgeConfig.title: BridgeConfig

DispatcherConfig.description:
[dispatcher] section in hal0.toml.

``extra="forbid"`` (P3-schema Part C): a leaf tunable table.

admission_wait_timeout_s.description: Max seconds a request may wait in a slot's admission queue (hal0.dispatcher.admission; only applies to slots with max_inflight set) before the dispatcher gives up and returns 503 with Retry-After, rather than forwarding. The read-timeout clock for the forward itself starts only after admission, so this bound is independent of [dispatcher].direct_read_timeout_s.
admission_wait_timeout_s.title: Admission Wait Timeout S

direct_read_timeout_s.description: Non-streaming upstream read timeout in seconds. Large consolidation/extraction prompts can exceed 60s on slow slots. Streaming requests disable this per-request while the stall guard is active so the guard owns the body bound; it still bounds the wait for response headers on those requests, since the guard's own clocks only start once headers arrive. With both stall-guard bounds set to 0 it applies per body read as the transport backstop. Range 30-600.
direct_read_timeout_s.title: Direct Read Timeout S

stream_idle_timeout_s.description: Stall guard: max gap between two chunks of a relayed upstream stream before hal0 cuts it off. Must stay above the slowest expected prompt-processing silence on a cold CPU slot. 0 disables the bound.
stream_idle_timeout_s.title: Stream Idle Timeout S

stream_total_timeout_s.description: Stall guard: max wall-clock duration of a relayed upstream stream before hal0 cuts it off and emits a terminal diagnostic chunk. Without this a chatty never-terminating upstream is relayed forever — each chunk resets the transport read timer (#1893). Note this is wall clock: a healthy long generation on slow hardware that outlives the budget is also cut. 0 disables the bound.
stream_total_timeout_s.title: Stream Total Timeout S

DispatcherConfig.title: DispatcherConfig

MemoryCompatConfig.description:
[memory.compat] section of hal0.toml.

The engine-compatible memory endpoint for coding agents,
``/api/memory/compat`` (ADR-0058 decision 4b).

gitlog_min_interval_s.description: The shortest time between two retains of one project's commit-log document (strategy 'gitlog'). The plugin re-sends its last 300 commit messages as one document whenever a session starts on a HEAD it has not sent, and every worktree and branch has its own HEAD. The engine matches stored chunks by position, so one new commit at the top changes every chunk and the whole document is extracted again: hours of the memory model's time on a local slot. A commit-log retain sooner than this after the last one accepted here is answered 429 with Retry-After; the plugin logs it and carries on. After a restart of hal0-api the stored document's last write in the engine counts as the last retain. 0 turns the limit off.
gitlog_min_interval_s.title: Gitlog Min Interval S

max_concurrent_recalls.description: How many recalls through the endpoint may run at once, across all clients. One client is always limited to two. A request over the limit is answered 429 with Retry-After.
max_concurrent_recalls.title: Max Concurrent Recalls

max_concurrent_reflects.description: How many reflects through the endpoint may run at once, across all clients. A reflect holds the memory engine's language model for minutes; this keeps coding agents from starving hal0's own agents of it. One client is always limited to one at a time, and the endpoint never runs more than one fewer than [memory.lanes] lets the engine run (one, when the engine runs one). A request over the limit is answered 429 with Retry-After.
max_concurrent_reflects.title: Max Concurrent Reflects

max_item_bytes.description: The largest 'content' of one retained item, in UTF-8 bytes. The largest thing the plugin sends is a whole session transcript. The request body is capped at 48 MiB whatever this is set to.
max_item_bytes.title: Max Item Bytes

max_outstanding_bytes.description: The most bytes of unfinished asynchronous retains one client may have submitted. A single retain is always accepted when the client has nothing outstanding.
max_outstanding_bytes.title: Max Outstanding Bytes

max_outstanding_operations.description: How many asynchronous retains one client may have submitted that the engine has not finished. An async retain is accepted at once and extracted later, so without this one client could fill the engine's queue. A session submits one retain per turn and the plugin polls ten at a time; a first-time repository ingest (the plugin's default is 300 commits) is slowed by this limit, not refused: the next retain is answered 429 with Retry-After until earlier ones finish.
max_outstanding_operations.title: Max Outstanding Operations

shared_document_prefixes.description: Document-id prefixes whose documents every client of a project shares. A client's documents are otherwise stored in a namespace of its own, so one client cannot replace another's. An id that starts with one of these is stored in the project's shared namespace instead and any client of that project may write it. The default is the ids the Hindsight coding-agents plugin derives from the repository itself: one commit (git:), the commit log (gitlog:) and a codebase-survey marker (survey-baseline:). Setting this key replaces the default list; an empty list shares nothing.
shared_document_prefixes.title: Shared Document Prefixes

MemoryCompatConfig.title: MemoryCompatConfig

MemoryConfig.description:
[memory] section of hal0.toml.

Container for the per-subsystem memory tunables. Carries
``[memory.graph]``, ``[memory.embedding]``, ``[memory.priority]``,
``[memory.models]``, ``[memory.decision]``, ``[memory.lanes]``,
``[memory.console]`` (Hindsight 1.2 showcase additions) and
``[memory.projects]`` (the project registry, ADR-0058). Future memory
features (retention, prune-policy, archival) land under this single
namespace rather than scattering top-level tables.

bank.description: Name of the Hindsight bank behind the 'shared' namespace, where every agent's durable memory lives (ADR-0052, ADR-0058 decision 7). The namespace grammar ('shared' | 'private:<agent>') is unchanged; only the bank id the provider talks to differs. A store hal0 wrote before the two-bank layout keeps the bank it has (recorded in /var/lib/hal0/state/memory-layout.json) until it is folded in, and there this key names a bank only when set to something other than 'hal0:shared'. Changing it points hal0-api at a different bank, so run 'hal0 memory migrate platform' first to clone the existing bank's data into the new name, then restart hal0-api.
bank.title: Bank

enabled.description: Whether the memory subsystem (Hindsight engine, /mcp/memory, /api/memory/*, the dashboard's Agent -> Memory tab) is built at startup. Replaces the old HAL0_MEMORY_ENABLED env var — toggle via 'hal0 memory enable' / 'hal0 memory disable'. Consumed once at create_app(), so a change needs a hal0-api restart.
enabled.title: Enabled

engine.description: Active memory engine. 'hindsight' (default) is the platform engine; 'pgvector' is the in-memory, non-durable fallback. 'mem0' is accepted but not implemented: hal0 logs a warning and runs Hindsight. The legacy 'cognee' value was retired in v1.0.0 (the Cognee store has been dark since v0.4 and its wrapper was removed) — a hal0.toml still carrying it must be updated to 'hindsight'.
engine.title: Engine

private_bank.description: Name of the Hindsight bank behind every 'private:<agent>' namespace in the two-bank layout (ADR-0058 decision 7): one bank for all agents, where each agent's 'agent:<id>' tag scopes it to its own memory. Must differ from [memory] bank. Not used by a store still on its pre-two-bank layout. Needs a hal0-api restart.
private_bank.title: Private Bank

public_url.description: The URL coding agents should reach the Hindsight engine at, e.g. through a reverse proxy. Used by the GET /api/memory/agents install one-liner in place of guessing <request host>:9177 when set.
public_url.title: Public Url

MemoryConfig.title: MemoryConfig

MemoryConsoleConfig.description:
[memory.console] section of hal0.toml — the Hindsight Control Plane.

Optional power-user UI (``@vectorize-io/hindsight-control-plane`` on
node, verified as ``hal0-memory-console.service`` on CT143). Gated off
by default: node may not be present on a given box, in which case the
installer must skip install with a clear doctor warning rather than
failing the run.

bind.description: Bind address — kept loopback by default; proxy through hal0-api.
bind.title: Bind

enabled.description: Install/run the Hindsight Control Plane service.
enabled.title: Enabled

port.description: Port the Hindsight Control Plane binds; changing it moves the console link.
port.title: Port

MemoryConsoleConfig.title: MemoryConsoleConfig

MemoryConsolidationLaneConfig.description: ``[memory.lanes.consolidation]``: the per-op lane plus the batch size.

batch_size.description: HINDSIGHT_API_CONSOLIDATION_LLM_BATCH_SIZE (#3762): memories consolidated per LLM call (1 = no batching). The engine's own default is 8, which can overflow the 8192-token output cap hal0 renders; a batch that overflows is split and retried, and what still fails is counted as failed. Unset means hal0's default, 4 (DEFAULT_CONSOLIDATION_BATCH_SIZE), resolved when the drop-in is rendered so a save never pins it.
batch_size.title: Batch Size

max_completion_tokens.description: Hard cap on one LLM call's output tokens (#3596): HINDSIGHT_API_CONSOLIDATION_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS for consolidation, HINDSIGHT_API_REFLECT_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS for reflect (which also bounds mental-model refresh, a reflect call). Unset means 8192 for consolidation and reflect; 0 leaves the engine uncapped. Valid only on consolidation and reflect; retain is capped by [memory.graph].extraction_max_tokens, and Hindsight has no separate mental-model-refresh cap.
max_completion_tokens.title: Max Completion Tokens

max_concurrent.description: HINDSIGHT_API_{OP}_LLM_MAX_CONCURRENT. Unset falls back to [memory.lanes].llm_max_concurrent (itself defaulting to [memory.graph].extraction_max_concurrent; consolidation takes one fewer).
max_concurrent.title: Max Concurrent

virtual_model.description: Optional per-op hal0 virtual model override (e.g. 'hal0/utility' for a burst lane) instead of the shared 'hal0/memory' alias.
virtual_model.title: Virtual Model

MemoryConsolidationLaneConfig.title: MemoryConsolidationLaneConfig

MemoryDecisionConfig.description:
[memory.decision] section of hal0.toml — the Hindsight 1.2 decision model.

The decision model (``hs-decide-1-flash``) replaces many of Hindsight's
LLM calls (recall rank/prune/dedup, consolidation judgments, reflect
sufficiency, page delta gating) with a single cheap forward pass.

``provider`` is ``"off"`` (the default), ``"local"`` or
``"hindsight-cloud"``. ``"local"`` is the CPU ``hal0-hs-decide`` service on
``port``, built by the opt-in ``memory-decision`` component
(``hal0 memory decision install``, :mod:`hal0.memory.decision_component`),
which also sets ``provider = "local"``. The showcase drop-in points
hindsight-api at it only while its unit is installed (#3519,
``hal0.memory.extraction_env.decision_engine_base_url``), and renders the
engine-side provider value ``hindsight`` plus a fixed placeholder API key
(the engine wants a non-empty key even for a loopback URL). A
``hal0.toml`` that says ``provider = "local"`` explicitly keeps that value.

base_url.description: Override for where hal0 proxies POST /v1/systemone. Unset means http://127.0.0.1:<port> (the local hal0-hs-decide service).
base_url.title: Base Url

enabled.description: Whether the decision model lane is enabled at all.
enabled.title: Enabled

max_request_tokens.description: HINDSIGHT_API_DECISION_MODEL_MAX_REQUEST_TOKENS — CPU latency budget cap; measured ~25s @ 8.5k tokens on shared CPU.
max_request_tokens.title: Max Request Tokens

port.description: Port the local hal0-hs-decide service binds.
port.title: Port

provider.description: 'off' (the default: the engine uses its LLM lane for decision-gated operations), 'local' (the hal0-hs-decide service that `hal0 memory decision install` builds), or 'hindsight-cloud' (hosted decision model).
provider.title: Provider

threads.description: CPU thread count for the local hal0-hs-decide server.
threads.title: Threads

MemoryDecisionConfig.title: MemoryDecisionConfig

MemoryEmbeddingConfig.description:
[memory.embedding] section of hal0.toml — Hindsight-era fallback-rerank knobs.

ADR-0023 made Hindsight the platform memory engine. Hindsight embeds
server-side with its own bundled model, so hal0 no longer pins an
embedding model here; what remains configurable is the FALLBACK
reranker hal0 runs over cross-bank recall results when the engine
returned no ``scores.final`` for any of them
(:class:`hal0.memory.hindsight_provider.Hal0Reranker`):

  - ``rerank_fallback`` — switch the fallback off entirely.
  - ``rerank_gateway_url`` — the OpenAI-surface gateway the reranker
    POSTs ``/v1/rerankings`` to (hal0-api's dispatcher, which routes
    to the rerank slot).
  - ``rerank_model`` — optional override of the rerank model id sent
    in the request body; empty means the model the ``rerank`` slot is
    bound to.
  - ``rerank_connect_timeout_s`` / ``rerank_read_timeout_s`` — the
    HTTP budgets; failures fall through to fused vector ordering,
    never blocking recall.

The cognee-era fields (``model``, ``rerank_enabled``, ``rerank_url``,
``rerank_over_fetch_factor``, ``rerank_max_candidates``) were removed
with the cognee wrapper; ``extra = "ignore"`` silently drops them
from an older hal0.toml on load (gone on next save), mirroring how
ADR-0023 retired ``[memory.graph]``'s ``route``/``upstream``.

rerank_connect_timeout_s.description: TCP connect timeout for the rerank HTTP call. Kept short so a wedged rerank slot can't stall memory_search; the read budget is the larger of the two knobs.
rerank_connect_timeout_s.title: Rerank Connect Timeout S

rerank_fallback.description: Run the fallback reranker when recall results carry no engine score (an engine without ``scores.final``). It is skipped with no network call while the ``rerank`` slot serves no model.
rerank_fallback.title: Rerank Fallback

rerank_gateway_url.description: Base URL of the OpenAI-compatible gateway the memory reranker calls (``POST {url}/v1/rerankings``). Defaults to hal0-api itself, whose dispatcher routes to the rerank slot.
rerank_gateway_url.title: Rerank Gateway Url

rerank_model.description: Rerank model id sent to the gateway. Empty (the default) sends the model the ``rerank`` slot is bound to. Set it only to override that; it must resolve to a model the slot serves.
rerank_model.title: Rerank Model

rerank_read_timeout_s.description: Read budget for the rerank slot. Default raised from the previous shared 2.0s scalar because GPU rerank under concurrent load (CPU oversubscription stalls responses) regularly breaches a tight total budget, which silently falls through to vector ordering. Failures still fall through — this just stops spurious timeouts under healthy-but-loaded conditions.
rerank_read_timeout_s.title: Rerank Read Timeout S

MemoryEmbeddingConfig.title: MemoryEmbeddingConfig

MemoryGraphConfig.description:
[memory.graph] section of hal0.toml (ADR-0023).

Controls graph extraction on the Hindsight engine. Hindsight builds its graph
natively via its own extraction LLM; hal0 points that LLM at the fixed
virtual id ``hal0/memory`` (through a systemd drop-in) and resolves it on
every call to ``hal0/<extraction_slot>`` or, when set, to
``extraction_model`` (#2919), so the engine's model changes without a
restart.

ADR-0023 replaced the inert, cognee-era ``route``/``upstream`` enum with a
single ``extraction_slot`` knob. ``model_config.extra = "ignore"`` means a
lingering ``route``/``upstream`` key in an old hal0.toml is silently dropped on
load (and gone on the next save) rather than failing validation.

consolidation_reserved_slots.description: Worker slots only consolidation may use (HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_CONSOLIDATION_RESERVED_SLOTS). 2 is Hindsight's own default. A floor, not a cap. Applied via the hindsight-api drop-in; the daemon restarts to pick it up.
consolidation_reserved_slots.title: Consolidation Reserved Slots

enabled.description: Reporting gate for the graph-extraction status surface. Hindsight builds its graph natively, so this flag is informational on that engine; vector recall is unaffected either way.
enabled.title: Enabled

extraction_llm_retries.description: Retries of a single extraction LLM call inside one retain attempt (HINDSIGHT_API_RETAIN_LLM_MAX_RETRIES). Each retry can wait the full LLM timeout. Together with llm_timeout_s it fixes the retain wall limit hal0 writes as HINDSIGHT_API_RETAIN_WALL_TIMEOUT: Hindsight cancels a retain that runs past it and marks it failed without retrying. With per_call = llm_timeout_s x (extraction_llm_retries + 1), the limit is max(min(max(3600, 3 x per_call), 14400), per_call + llm_timeout_s) seconds: three worst-case calls, never below Hindsight's own 3600 s, capped at 4 h so one document cannot hold the single extraction lane longer (only a per-call budget already past the cap raises it), and always strictly above one call so a call is never cut mid-flight. Defaults give 3600 s. Applied via the hindsight-api drop-in; the daemon restarts to pick it up.
extraction_llm_retries.title: Extraction Llm Retries

extraction_max_concurrent.description: How many LLM calls Hindsight may have in flight at once against the extraction target (HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_MAX_CONCURRENT and HINDSIGHT_API_RETAIN_LLM_MAX_CONCURRENT). This also bounds consolidation, reflect and mental-model refresh. 1 serialises them; raise it only for a slot that genuinely serves parallel requests. hal0 holds the rendered value to the extraction slot's --parallel (calls beyond it queue inside llama-server and time out), keeps this setting as you wrote it, and warns on save and in graph status when it clamps. Applied via the hindsight-api drop-in; the daemon restarts to pick it up.
extraction_max_concurrent.title: Extraction Max Concurrent

extraction_max_tokens.description: Completion-token cap per extraction call (HINDSIGHT_API_RETAIN_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS). Bounds how long one call can run. Hindsight refuses every retain into a bank whose retain chunk size is not strictly below this cap: the engine default chunk is 3000 (which the 3072 floor clears), but the Hindsight coding-agent plugin sets 12000 on its bank strategies, hence the 16384 default. A larger cap lengthens each call on a small slot, so keep llm_timeout_s above the time one call takes. Applied via the hindsight-api drop-in; the daemon restarts to pick it up.
extraction_max_tokens.title: Extraction Max Tokens

extraction_model.description: Optional upstream model the memory engine runs on instead of the local extraction_slot (#2919): an id hal0's own /v1 already routes to a configured upstream, e.g. 'MiniMax-M2.5' or 'minimax/minimax-m3'. hindsight-api always calls the fixed virtual id hal0/memory; hal0 resolves that to this model when set, else to hal0/<extraction_slot>, so switching needs no engine restart. Validated against the live upstream catalogs by the API at set-time. Never a hal0/<slot> id — a local slot belongs in extraction_slot.
extraction_model.title: Extraction Model

extraction_retry_backoff_s.description: Seconds a failed queued memory task waits before it is requeued (HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_TASK_RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS), so a retry does not land on a slot that is still busy with the attempt that just timed out. Worker-wide like extraction_task_retries: every queued operation shares it. Applied via the hindsight-api drop-in; the daemon restarts to pick it up.
extraction_retry_backoff_s.title: Extraction Retry Backoff S

extraction_slot.description: The local llm slot Hindsight uses for graph extraction / consolidation / reflect while extraction_model is unset. hindsight-api calls the fixed id hal0/memory; hal0's /v1 resolves it to this slot per call, falling back to agent when memory has no bound model (ADR-0053), so a change needs no engine restart. Validated against the live enabled-llm-slot set by the API at set-time.
extraction_slot.title: Extraction Slot

extraction_task_retries.description: How many times a failed queued memory task is requeued before it is marked failed (HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_MAX_RETRIES) and shows under 'Retry failed' on the Memory page. Bounds the total time one document can occupy the slot. This is Hindsight's worker-wide setting: it applies to every queued operation (retain, consolidation, mental-model refresh), not only extraction. Applied via the hindsight-api drop-in; the daemon restarts to pick it up.
extraction_task_retries.title: Extraction Task Retries

extraction_worker_slots.description: How many queued memory tasks (retain, consolidation, mental-model refresh) the engine runs at once (HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_MAX_SLOTS). Independent of extraction_max_concurrent, which caps LLM calls: each running task also holds its chunks, embeddings and graph writes in memory. Hindsight's own default of 10 took the engine to several GiB resident and into the OOM killer on an 11 GiB box, so hal0 renders 4. Part of these slots is reserved per task type (retain_reserved_slots, consolidation_reserved_slots, refresh_reserved_slots); the rest is one shared pool any task may use, and the reservations must leave at least one slot in it. The floor is 3. Worker-wide like extraction_task_retries. Applied via the hindsight-api drop-in; the daemon restarts to pick it up.
extraction_worker_slots.title: Extraction Worker Slots

llm_timeout_s.description: Timeout (seconds) for the Hindsight daemon's LLM calls — extraction, consolidation, and reflect. Covers cold slot starts and long reflects. Propagated to hindsight-api as HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_TIMEOUT via the same systemd drop-in as the extraction slot; the daemon restarts to pick it up. It also sets the retain wall limit (HINDSIGHT_API_RETAIN_WALL_TIMEOUT, which hal0 derives, see extraction_llm_retries): the wall limit is always above llm_timeout_s x (extraction_llm_retries + 1). Hindsight sends these calls non-streaming through hal0's /v1, so hal0 also uses this value as the read timeout for hal0/memory requests when it is longer than [dispatcher].direct_read_timeout_s; a shorter value never lowers that setting.
llm_timeout_s.title: Llm Timeout S

refresh_reserved_slots.description: Worker slots only knowledge-page (mental model) refreshes may use (HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_REFRESH_MENTAL_MODEL_RESERVED_SLOTS). 0, Hindsight's own default, leaves refreshes to the shared pool. A floor, not a cap. Applied via the hindsight-api drop-in; the daemon restarts to pick it up.
refresh_reserved_slots.title: Refresh Reserved Slots

retain_reserved_slots.description: Worker slots only retains may use (HINDSIGHT_API_WORKER_RETAIN_RESERVED_SLOTS), so new memories are stored even while page refreshes or consolidation hold every shared slot. A floor, not a cap: retains also use free shared slots. When hal0.toml does not set it and extraction_worker_slots has no room for it (3 slots with consolidation's 2), it is 0 instead of 1. Applied via the hindsight-api drop-in; the daemon restarts to pick it up.
retain_reserved_slots.title: Retain Reserved Slots

MemoryGraphConfig.title: MemoryGraphConfig

MemoryLaneOpConfig.description:
Per-operation LLM lane override under ``[memory.lanes.<op>]``.

One of ``retain``, ``consolidation``, ``reflect``, ``mental_model_refresh``.
Any field left unset falls back to the lane's global default
(:class:`MemoryLanesConfig`).

max_completion_tokens.description: Hard cap on one LLM call's output tokens (#3596): HINDSIGHT_API_CONSOLIDATION_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS for consolidation, HINDSIGHT_API_REFLECT_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS for reflect (which also bounds mental-model refresh, a reflect call). Unset means 8192 for consolidation and reflect; 0 leaves the engine uncapped. Valid only on consolidation and reflect; retain is capped by [memory.graph].extraction_max_tokens, and Hindsight has no separate mental-model-refresh cap.
max_completion_tokens.title: Max Completion Tokens

max_concurrent.description: HINDSIGHT_API_{OP}_LLM_MAX_CONCURRENT. Unset falls back to [memory.lanes].llm_max_concurrent (itself defaulting to [memory.graph].extraction_max_concurrent; consolidation takes one fewer).
max_concurrent.title: Max Concurrent

virtual_model.description: Optional per-op hal0 virtual model override (e.g. 'hal0/utility' for a burst lane) instead of the shared 'hal0/memory' alias.
virtual_model.title: Virtual Model

MemoryLaneOpConfig.title: MemoryLaneOpConfig

MemoryLanesConfig.description:
[memory.lanes] section of hal0.toml — global + per-op LLM concurrency lanes.

Fixes H0-98: hindsight-api caps ALL LLM calls process-wide via
``HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_MAX_CONCURRENT`` (engine default 32), but hal0 only
ever rendered the retain-bucket variant, so consolidation / reflect /
mental-model-refresh calls queued behind the memory slot's own
concurrency and could outlast the dispatcher's read timeout. This
section is the single hal0-rendered source for the global cap AND every
per-op override, retiring the hand-maintained
``zz-h0-98-llm-global-cap.conf`` drop-in.

llm_max_concurrent.description: HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_MAX_CONCURRENT — the GLOBAL cap across every hindsight-api LLM call (retain, consolidation, reflect, mental-model-refresh together), independent of any per-op cap. Unset follows [memory.graph].extraction_max_concurrent (as held to the extraction slot's --parallel), so the one setting the dashboard edits drives the whole engine, and the consolidation lane then takes one fewer so retain and page refresh always have a permit. An explicit value is still held to that same ceiling.
llm_max_concurrent.title: Llm Max Concurrent

MemoryLanesConfig.title: MemoryLanesConfig

MemoryModelsConfig.description:
[memory.models] section of hal0.toml — Hindsight 1.2 embed/rerank models.

hindsight-api 1.2.0 ships its own first-party local embedding/reranker
models (``hs-embed-1`` / ``hs-rerank-1``, both CPU, in-process). Defaults
here match the verified showcase env (``zz-showcase-1.2.conf``): local
CPU models, no external gateway hop. Rendered into
``HINDSIGHT_API_EMBEDDINGS_*`` / ``HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_*`` env by the
installer/extraction_env drop-in renderer.

The reranker can also run off-process (#3717): ``reranker_provider =
"litellm"`` with ``reranker_base_url`` / ``reranker_api_model`` sends the
Cohere-style rerank call to any compatible endpoint, hal0's own
``/v1/rerank`` (the ``rerank`` slot) included; ``"tei"`` targets a
text-embeddings-inference server; ``"rrf"`` turns cross-encoder scoring
off. ``reranker_max_candidates`` caps how much of each recall is scored.

reranker_api_model.description: HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_LITELLM_MODEL — the model id sent in each rerank request. Required for 'litellm'; for hal0's own endpoint, a model the rerank slot serves.
reranker_api_model.title: Reranker Api Model

reranker_base_url.description: Remote reranker endpoint. 'litellm': the base the engine POSTs {base}/rerank to in the Cohere wire format — http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 is hal0's own rerank slot. 'tei': the text-embeddings-inference server URL. Required for both, ignored for 'local' and 'rrf'. No credentials in the URL.
reranker_base_url.title: Reranker Base Url

reranker_local_batch_size.description: HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_LOCAL_BATCH_SIZE — pairs per predict() call (engine default 32). 'local' provider only.
reranker_local_batch_size.title: Reranker Local Batch Size

reranker_local_max_concurrent.description: HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_LOCAL_MAX_CONCURRENT — concurrent local rerank calls (engine default 4). 'local' provider only.
reranker_local_max_concurrent.title: Reranker Local Max Concurrent

reranker_local_timeout_s.description: HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_LOCAL_TIMEOUT — ceiling for one recall's local rerank, seconds (engine default 300; 0 disables). 'local' provider only.
reranker_local_timeout_s.title: Reranker Local Timeout S

reranker_max_candidates.description: HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_MAX_CANDIDATES — how many recall candidates the reranker scores. The engine default is 300, which costs 30-40 s per recall on the CPU cross-encoder; 60 keeps recall under a second.
reranker_max_candidates.title: Reranker Max Candidates

reranker_max_candidates_low.description: HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_MAX_CANDIDATES_LOW — cap for low-budget recalls. Unset uses reranker_max_candidates.
reranker_max_candidates_low.title: Reranker Max Candidates Low

reranker_timeout_s.description: Remote reranker HTTP timeout, seconds: HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_LITELLM_TIMEOUT (engine default 60) or HINDSIGHT_API_RERANKER_TEI_HTTP_TIMEOUT (engine default 30).
reranker_timeout_s.title: Reranker Timeout S

MemoryModelsConfig.title: MemoryModelsConfig

MemoryPriorityConfig.description:
[memory.priority] shared-memory scheduling settings (ADR-0053).

Config contract only: request admission and preemption are implemented
separately. Upgrades explicitly opt out via migration v4.

quiet_gap_s.description: Quiet time after chat, in seconds.
quiet_gap_s.title: Quiet Gap S

MemoryPriorityConfig.title: MemoryPriorityConfig

MemoryProjectsConfig.description:
[memory.projects] section of hal0.toml — the project registry.

ADR-0058 decision 4a: hal0 resolves the project of a memory write to one
slug before it tags the write (``hal0.memory.projects.resolve_project``).
This table is what the resolver consults. Every entry is normalised at
load with the resolver's own spelling rule, so ``My Repo`` and ``my-repo``
are the same name.

aliases.description: Other spellings of a project: a name on the left is tagged as the project on the right (for example a repository's directory name that differs from the project's name). Applied before the deny list. An alias may not point at a denied name or back at a name that leads to it. An entry whose two sides are the same name once normalised does nothing and is ignored.
aliases.title: Aliases

deny.description: Names that are never projects: directory names a client reports when it is not inside a repository. A write naming one is stored with no project. Setting this key replaces the default list.
deny.title: Deny

registered.description: Project names the operator has confirmed. Writes are accepted for any name; 'hal0 doctor' (memory_projects) reports names in use that are neither listed here nor aliased.
registered.title: Registered

MemoryProjectsConfig.title: MemoryProjectsConfig

MemoryReflectLaneConfig.description: ``[memory.lanes.reflect]``: the per-op lane plus the reflect wall clock.

max_completion_tokens.description: Hard cap on one LLM call's output tokens (#3596): HINDSIGHT_API_CONSOLIDATION_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS for consolidation, HINDSIGHT_API_REFLECT_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS for reflect (which also bounds mental-model refresh, a reflect call). Unset means 8192 for consolidation and reflect; 0 leaves the engine uncapped. Valid only on consolidation and reflect; retain is capped by [memory.graph].extraction_max_tokens, and Hindsight has no separate mental-model-refresh cap.
max_completion_tokens.title: Max Completion Tokens

max_concurrent.description: HINDSIGHT_API_{OP}_LLM_MAX_CONCURRENT. Unset falls back to [memory.lanes].llm_max_concurrent (itself defaulting to [memory.graph].extraction_max_concurrent; consolidation takes one fewer).
max_concurrent.title: Max Concurrent

virtual_model.description: Optional per-op hal0 virtual model override (e.g. 'hal0/utility' for a burst lane) instead of the shared 'hal0/memory' alias.
virtual_model.title: Virtual Model

wall_timeout_s.description: HINDSIGHT_API_REFLECT_WALL_TIMEOUT (#3759): seconds the engine gives one reflect, and one knowledge-page refresh (a reflect call), from start to finish. For a reflect the clock includes time spent waiting for an LLM permit. For a refresh it stops while a call waits for one (hindsight-api 1.2.3; one wait can add at most this many seconds), so a refresh queued behind consolidation and retain is no longer cancelled for the queue. The engine's own default is 300. Unset means hal0's default, 1800 (DEFAULT_REFLECT_WALL_TIMEOUT_S), resolved when the drop-in is rendered so a save never pins it. Keep it above [memory.graph].llm_timeout_s: a wall clock shorter than one LLM call's timeout cannot let a slow call finish.
wall_timeout_s.title: Wall Timeout S

MemoryReflectLaneConfig.title: MemoryReflectLaneConfig

MemoryRefreshConfig.description:
[memory.refresh] section of hal0.toml.

When the memory engine refreshes knowledge pages (its mental models) and
when it consolidates (ADR-0060). hal0 writes the page settings onto every
page of this box's banks and onto the banks' defaults, and overrides
whatever a page writer asks for, so one setting holds for every page.

consolidation.description: When the engine consolidates new facts into observations. 'continuous' consolidates as facts arrive and keeps up with intake. 'scheduled' turns the engine's own consolidation off for this box's banks and has hal0-api start one run on the schedule below, so the memory model is idle the rest of the day; recall sees new facts at once, observations only after the run.
consolidation.title: Consolidation

consolidation_schedule.description: The schedule consolidation runs on when consolidation is 'scheduled': a five-field cron expression in UTC. The default is daily at 02:00 UTC, an hour before the default page refresh.
consolidation_schedule.title: Consolidation Schedule

min_interval_s.description: The shortest time between two automatic refreshes of one page, in seconds. A refresh due sooner waits until the time is up. Written to every page and to the banks' default. A refresh asked for by hand is not held back. 0 turns the floor off.
min_interval_s.title: Min Interval S

pages.description: When knowledge pages refresh. 'scheduled' refreshes each page on the schedule below, and only when facts in its scope changed since its last refresh. 'after_consolidation' refreshes a page after every consolidation round that touched its scope: pages stay current, but each refresh is several minutes of the memory model's time and a busy box can spend most of it on refreshes. 'manual' never refreshes a page by itself; a refresh runs only when one is asked for. Applies to every page, whatever the page asked for when it was written.
pages.title: Pages

schedule.description: The schedule pages refresh on when pages is 'scheduled': a five-field cron expression in UTC (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week). The default is daily at 03:00 UTC. A page whose facts have not changed skips the tick.
schedule.title: Schedule

MemoryRefreshConfig.title: MemoryRefreshConfig

MetaConfig.description:
[meta] section in hal0.toml.  Tracks config schema version for migrations.

``extra="forbid"`` (P3-schema Part C): a leaf tunable table with no
legitimate unknown key — see PLAN.md §5 Tier 1 ("backend = vukan raises
with the field path"), which only holds if leaf tables reject typos.

schema_version.description: Config schema version.  hal0 config migrate bumps this when applying versioned transforms.  See PLAN.md §5 Tier 3.
schema_version.title: Schema Version

MetaConfig.title: MetaConfig

auto_scan_on_start.description: Run the discovery scan during app startup.
auto_scan_on_start.title: Auto Scan On Start

file_extensions.description: Filename suffixes treated as candidate model files (lowercase, includes the dot).
file_extensions.title: File Extensions

flm_store.description: Where FLM (NPU backend) model weights live. The NPU slot container bind-mounts this directory over FLM's hardcoded ~/.config/flm/models cache, and the host ``flm`` probe/pull bookkeeping points at it. Empty falls back to the HAL0_FLM_MODELS_DIR env var, then to FLM's default cache under the hal0 HOME (/var/lib/hal0/.config/flm/models). Set an absolute path (e.g. /mnt/ai-models/flm/models) to keep NPU weights off the root filesystem; hal0 creates the directory (container-uid-writable) at slot-spec build time and the generated unit orders after the backing mount, so a reboot with a late or missing mount no longer kills the slot with podman exit 125.
flm_store.title: Flm Store

pull_root.description: DEPRECATED — superseded by ``[models].store``. Retained so PR #313 installs round-trip without a manual edit. When ``store`` is set the pull engine ignores this field; clearing ``store`` falls back to ``pull_root`` so an operator who hand-edited their TOML pre-store still works. Will be removed in a future release.
pull_root.title: Pull Root

roots.description: Filesystem roots scanned for downloaded model files. Each must be an absolute path; non-existent paths are skipped at scan time. Default tracks HAL0_HOME for dev installs.
roots.title: Roots

store.description: Single source of truth for where hal0 reads + writes model files. When set (absolute path, e.g. ``/mnt/ai-models``), the pull engine writes here AND slot containers bind-mount the path identical-path with an SELinux relabel (observed on the next slot restart; see ``paths.model_store_root``). ``HAL0_MODEL_STORE`` env overrides it. Empty falls back to ``pull_root`` for PR-#313 compatibility, which itself defaults to ``paths.models_dir()``; note the mount default stays ``/mnt/ai-models`` (not ``pull_root``) so existing deployments are unaffected until ``store`` is set.
store.title: Store

NetworkConfig.description:
``[network]`` — how browsers reach this box, beyond the installer's view (#2382).

The Origin gate in ``hal0.api.auth`` (REST calls and WebSocket
upgrades alike) accepts the
``HAL0_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`` list the installer derives into the managed
``api.env`` block. That block is rewritten on every installer run, so an
origin hand-added there was lost on the next re-run. These keys are the
persisted, operator-owned additions: :func:`allowed_origins` merges the
origin of ``public_url`` and every ``extra_origins`` entry on top of the
env list at runtime. The installer never copies them into the managed
block, so removing one here revokes it on the next request.

Out of scope on purpose: the bind host, port and hostname stay in the
managed ``api.env`` block, because the systemd unit and avahi read them
before Python runs.

``extra="forbid"`` (P3-schema Part C leaf-table policy, same as
``[security]``): a typo'd key must fail loudly, not silently leave an
origin out of the allowlist.

comfyui_listen.description: Where ComfyUI's own web UI (the img slot, port 8188) answers. ``lan`` (the default) binds the LAN so other machines reach the editor at http://<host>:8188 or http://<host>.local:8188 — the Discovery (mDNS) card can announce it like Open WebUI. ComfyUI has no sign-in of its own: anyone on the network can queue workflows and read what it rendered. ``loopback`` fences the port to 127.0.0.1 like every other slot (the box itself, an SSH tunnel, or a reverse proxy you run with HAL0_COMFYUI_PUBLIC_URL). Applies at the next `hal0 slot restart img`.
comfyui_listen.title: Comfyui Listen

extra_origins.description: Other browser origins allowed to make state-changing requests and WebSocket upgrades, on top of HAL0_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: a second proxy, a MagicDNS name, http://box.lan:8080. Each entry is scheme://host[:port] with http or https and no path, stored without a trailing slash and deduplicated. Applies on the next request, no restart.
extra_origins.title: Extra Origins

public_url.description: The URL users reach hal0 at through a reverse proxy, e.g. https://hal0.example.com. Must be an absolute http or https URL. Its origin (scheme://host[:port]) is added to the browser-origin allowlist on top of HAL0_ALLOWED_ORIGINS. Applies on the next request, no restart. Unset = no reverse proxy.
public_url.title: Public Url

NetworkConfig.title: NetworkConfig

OpenWebUIConfig.description:
``[openwebui]`` — how hal0 treats requests that arrive from Open WebUI.

``extra="forbid"`` (P3-schema Part C leaf-table policy, same as ``[bridge]``):
a typo'd key must fail loudly instead of silently leaving the flag on.

hermes_session_from_chat_id.description: For a request to a Hermes-profile model that carries X-OpenWebUI-Chat-Id: send X-Hermes-Session-Id: owui-<chat id> to Hermes when the client sent no session header (one Open WebUI chat is one Hermes session), and drop `tools` and `tool_choice` from the body, because Hermes already has memory and admin tools of its own. Off = every request to Hermes is relayed unchanged. Applies to the next request.
hermes_session_from_chat_id.title: Hermes Session From Chat Id

OpenWebUIConfig.title: OpenWebUIConfig

RealtimeConfig.description:
``[realtime]`` — the OpenAI-Realtime WebSocket surface (HP-realtime inc-1).

Tunes the ``WS /v1/realtime`` endpoint: which local slots serve STT/TTS, the
fixed pcm16 sample rate, the in-process energy-VAD thresholds (server-VAD
turn detection — user decision 1), the output audio frame size, and the
voice-bounded approval wait.

``enabled`` is a hard kill switch. ``sample_rate`` is fixed at 24 kHz for the
MVP (matches the demo client's ``-sample-rate 24000`` and kokoro's native
pcm output — no resample either direction). ``stt_model`` / ``tts_model`` /
``tts_voice`` name the loaded slots the gateway calls over loopback (empty
``stt_model``/``tts_model`` falls back to the session's chat model, empty
``tts_voice`` lets the tts slot's own default apply).

VAD (``vad_*``): a zero-dependency energy-RMS detector (the venv has no
onnxruntime/webrtcvad/silero; adding them would pull a heavy dep + an
unpullable multi-file model — spec §2d). ``vad_energy_threshold`` is
normalized RMS (0-1); ``vad_silence_ms`` of trailing silence ends a turn;
a segment shorter than ``vad_min_speech_ms`` of voiced audio is treated as
noise and does not fire a turn. A silero backend can replace it in
increment 2 without touching these knobs' meaning.

``approval_wait_s`` bounds how long a gated steward tool may leave the voice
session silent before the assistant speaks a "still waiting — approve at the
bell" notice and ends the turn (the brain's own SSE would otherwise block up
to 300s — spec §2b / user decision 3). ``frame_ms`` is the output audio
frame size (``response.output_audio.delta`` granularity).

``extra="forbid"`` (P3-schema Part C): a leaf tunable table — a typo'd key
must fail loudly at load, never silently no-op.

approval_wait_s.description: How long a gated steward tool may leave the voice session silent before the assistant speaks a 'still waiting' notice and ends the turn, instead of blocking up to 300s.
approval_wait_s.title: Approval Wait S

default_model.description: Fallback chat model for a realtime session when neither stt_model nor tts_model names one.
default_model.title: Default Model

enabled.description: Hard kill switch for the WS /v1/realtime voice endpoint.
enabled.title: Enabled

frame_ms.description: Output audio frame size (ms) — the response.output_audio.delta granularity.
frame_ms.title: Frame Ms

max_buffer_seconds.description: Cap on buffered audio (seconds) held for a single realtime turn.
max_buffer_seconds.title: Max Buffer Seconds

sample_rate.description: Fixed pcm16 sample rate (Hz). 24 kHz matches the demo client and kokoro's native output — changing this does not resample either direction, so a mismatched client will hear distorted audio.
sample_rate.title: Sample Rate

stt_model.description: Loaded slot the gateway calls over loopback for speech-to-text. Empty falls back to the session's chat model.
stt_model.title: Stt Model

tts_model.description: Loaded slot the gateway calls over loopback for text-to-speech.
tts_model.title: Tts Model

tts_voice.description: Voice name passed to the tts slot. Empty lets the slot's own default apply.
tts_voice.title: Tts Voice

vad_energy_threshold.description: Normalized RMS (0-1) above which incoming audio counts as speech for the zero-dependency energy-VAD turn detector.
vad_energy_threshold.title: Vad Energy Threshold

vad_min_speech_ms.description: Minimum voiced-audio duration (ms) to count as speech rather than noise; shorter segments never fire a turn.
vad_min_speech_ms.title: Vad Min Speech Ms

vad_silence_ms.description: Trailing silence (ms) that ends a voice turn.
vad_silence_ms.title: Vad Silence Ms

vad_window_ms.description: Analysis window size (ms) the energy-VAD detector evaluates at a time.
vad_window_ms.title: Vad Window Ms

RealtimeConfig.title: RealtimeConfig

SecurityConfig.description:
[security] section — persisted auth-enforcement posture (KB-1 / O19).

``require_auth`` is the durable enable/disable toggle the dashboard
Security page writes (``PUT /api/auth/require``). Its default is
``None`` = *unset*, which the runtime resolves to auth **OFF** — the
shipped posture as of the 2026-07-19 operator decision: hal0 runs
trusted-LAN-open by default, matching how the boxes are actually run.

This deliberately retires KB-1's bind-address / key-presence auto-on:
that auto-on armed enforcement on a 0.0.0.0 bind but the dashboard
shipped no login UI, so every route answered ``authentication
required`` and operators disabled auth wholesale (``HAL0_REQUIRE_AUTH=0``)
to use the product (docs/rework r4 finding O19). Auth is now
explicit-enable only.

Resolution precedence (see :func:`hal0.api.auth.require_auth_enabled`):
the ``HAL0_REQUIRE_AUTH`` env var wins over this persisted value, which
in turn wins over the OFF default.

``extra="forbid"`` (P3-schema Part C leaf-table policy, same as
``[brain_chat]``): a typo'd key in the SECURITY section must fail loudly
at load, never silently no-op an enforcement toggle.

require_auth.description: Persisted auth-enforcement toggle. None = unset → auth OFF (trusted-LAN open, the shipped default). True/False are explicit operator choices. Overridden at runtime by the HAL0_REQUIRE_AUTH env var.
require_auth.title: Require Auth

trust_forwarded_for.description: Honour X-Forwarded-For for the login/rotate rate limiter and caller-IP attribution instead of the raw TCP peer. None = unset → OFF (the raw peer is used — safe default, since a client can forge this header). Only enable when hal0 sits behind a reverse proxy known to strip/overwrite any client-supplied X-Forwarded-For (Traefik/nginx/Caddy do this by default) — otherwise every caller can pick its own rate-limit bucket by spoofing the header. Overridden at runtime by the HAL0_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR env var.
trust_forwarded_for.title: Trust Forwarded For

SecurityConfig.title: SecurityConfig

SlotsConfig.description:
[slots] section in hal0.toml.  Global slot policy.

``extra="forbid"`` (P3-schema Part C): a leaf tunable table.

default_images.description: Per-runner-family operator default-image overrides (runner-image-catalogue v2). Keys are hal0.runners.RUNNER_IMAGES family keys (standard, cpu, cuda, halogen, flm, kokoro, moonshine, qwen3tts, comfyui); values are full image refs (e.g. 'ghcr.io/hal0ai/hal0-runner-standard:<tag>'). A family listed here launches that ref instead of the release-baked default wherever no per-slot image_pin applies (hal0.providers.container._resolve_image_ref). CLEAR SEMANTICS: the settings PUT deep-merge has no key-delete idiom, so sending an explicit null value for a family removes the override (the validator drops null-valued keys); an empty string is rejected. Applies on the next slot (re)start.
default_images.title: Default Images

evict_pressure_mb.description: Host free-RAM floor (MiB) for pressure-driven eviction (#903, spec 2026-08-02). When host MemAvailable drops below this value, every non-pinned resident slot is a candidate, evicted in priority order (lowest `priority` first, least-recently-used as the tie-break within a tier) until free RAM is back above the floor. 0 disables pressure eviction. `pinned` is the only per-slot exemption — `idle_timeout_s = 0` on a slot does not exempt it from this path. The ComfyUI img-group slot is never a candidate.
evict_pressure_mb.title: Evict Pressure Mb

fabric_clock_guard.description: Policy when an NPU slot (device=npu, the `flm` recipe) would load alongside a GPU slot (vulkan/rocm/hip) that is up or loading, or vice versa, while the Proxmox host's AMD GPU fabric clock is not held at its top DPM level (hal0.slots.fabric_clock_guard; ROCm/TheRock#8709 — a fclk DPM change mid-flight can hang the box or corrupt NPU results on Strix Halo). `refuse` (default) blocks the load with the host-side fix in the error; `warn` logs and stores the warning on the slot like the GTT-leak check but still loads; `off` skips the check entirely. An unreadable fabric-clock state (expected inside hal0's own container — the sysfs write is host-only, but the read should still work) always warns, never refuses. Overridable per-process with HAL0_FABRIC_CLOCK_GUARD.
fabric_clock_guard.title: Fabric Clock Guard

idle_timeout_s.description: Default idle-TTL (seconds) for hard eviction, applied per slot when the slot's own TOML has no idle_timeout_s override. 0 disables IDLE-TTL eviction for slots using this default — pressure eviction and pre-load eviction are separate paths, exempted by `pinned`, not by this value. The ComfyUI img-group slot is never unloaded by idle, pressure or pre-load eviction.
idle_timeout_s.title: Idle Timeout S

max_slots.description: Maximum number of slots that may exist (creation gate; 0 = unlimited). Counts every slot TOML including the seeded ones (utility, rerank, tts, img, npu, …), so values below the current slot count block new-slot creation. Applies to the next slot creation — no restart needed.
max_slots.title: Max Slots

network_mode.description: Box-default podman network mode for slot containers (``Network=<mode>`` in the generated Quadlet). Empty (the default) means bridge networking with a loopback ``PublishPort`` — the safe default that keeps raw slot ports off the LAN behind hal0-api. Set to ``host`` on netns-limited substrates (unprivileged podman-in-LXC, where bridge netns teardown races leave slots unloadable) so every slot renders ``Network=host``. This is DEPLOY-TIME configuration for the box's substrate, not a runtime probe — the renderer never sniffs podman/LXC itself. SECURITY NOTE: host networking shares the container's loopback with hal0-api, so a host-net slot can reach 127.0.0.1 services on the CT (e.g. hal0-api itself); the compensating fence is that the slot process is force-bound to 127.0.0.1 (not 0.0.0.0) and every hal0-api route is auth-gated — the raw unauthenticated slot port is never LAN-reachable. This shared-loopback reach is the accepted residual (see docs/rework/podman-unprivileged-findings.md). A slot whose provider REQUIRES host net (ComfyUI) already forces it regardless of this default. Applies on the next slot (re)start.
network_mode.title: Network Mode

port_dnat_auto_repair.description: Let hal0 repair a MISSING netavark DNAT rule on its own (#3724): when a running slot fails /health because its published port has no DNAT rule reaching the container, or a slot start leaves another running container's port without one, run `podman network reload --all` (rebuilds every running container's rules, restarts nothing) at most once per 10 minutes box-wide, then re-probe. Stale rules are never auto-repaired. Set to false to only report (error_reason port_dnat_missing) and leave the repair to `hal0 doctor ports --fix`.
port_dnat_auto_repair.title: Port Dnat Auto Repair

port_range_end.description: Last port in the auto-allocation pool (inclusive). The default stops below 8188 so new slots never claim ComfyUI's port; the allocator also skips any port already used by an existing slot TOML. Applies to the next slot creation — no restart needed.
port_range_end.title: Port Range End

port_range_start.description: First port in the auto-allocation pool for new slots.
port_range_start.title: Port Range Start

preload_evict_enabled.description: Free memory SYNCHRONOUSLY before a load starts, when the incoming model's estimated footprint plus preload_evict_headroom_mb would not fit in projected free memory. Evicts non-pinned resident slots (never the ComfyUI img-group slot) in priority order (lowest `priority` first, least-recently-used as the tie-break within a tier) — the same eligibility evict_pressure_mb uses — until it fits, or fails the load with a clear error if it still doesn't fit after evicting everything eligible. Set to false to rely solely on the reactive pressure sweeper (#903), which only reacts after the fact on a timer.
preload_evict_enabled.title: Preload Evict Enabled

preload_evict_headroom_mb.description: Extra free-RAM slack (MiB) required on top of a model's estimated footprint before pre-load eviction (preload_evict_enabled) considers a load safe to start. Absorbs error in the coarse file-size + KV-cache footprint estimate and runtime/container overhead the estimate doesn't capture.
preload_evict_headroom_mb.title: Preload Evict Headroom Mb

publish_host.description: Host address slot containers publish their port on (``--publish=<host>:<port>:<port>``). Default ``127.0.0.1`` keeps slot ports loopback-only, reachable solely through hal0-api/Traefik — the safe default. Set to ``0.0.0.0`` to bind every slot on all interfaces so raw slot ports are reachable directly over the LAN (e.g. ``http://<host>.local:<port>``); this EXPOSES inference endpoints on your network, bypassing the API/reverse-proxy front door. A specific interface IP (e.g. ``192.0.2.10``) binds just that address. Applies on the next slot (re)start. Host-networked slots (``network_mode=host``) ignore this — port publishing is a no-op there.
publish_host.title: Publish Host

auto_restart_image_drift.description: At every hal0-api start, restart slots whose running container uses a different runner image than the one a fresh render would pick (a stale image keeps serving the build a release replaced). Slots with a request in flight, or whose activity cannot be read (no metrics endpoint, e.g. image/speech runtimes), are skipped. Argv-only drift is never restarted. Consumed once at startup, so a change needs a hal0-api restart.
auto_restart_image_drift.title: Auto Restart Image Drift
